scope: JEE Mains · Maths · Sequences and Series (221 PYQs screened, 218 pass)

exclusions.note: max a^5 b^3 c^2 d given a+b+c+d=11. Needs the 11-term weighted split (a/5 x5, b/3 x3, c/2 x2, d) or multivariable calculus; 3 degrees of freedom, so single-variable substitution does not close it. Audience meets AM-GM only as the 2-term a+b >= 2sqrt(ab) (12 NDA questions, all 2-term) and SB XI:11.6 proves A>=G>=H for TWO numbers.

y = x^2/2 + 2x^3/3 + 3x^4/4 + ... splits as a GP minus sum x^k/k; the second half is -log(1-x) and there is no GP-only route. SB XI:11.8 Power Series covers e^x, sin, cos expansions only; log(1+x) as a SERIES appears nowhere in NDA, MHT-CET or the SB Cl-11 bank (every log(1+x) hit is the function, in limits/integration).
3x^2/2 + 5x^3/3 + 7x^4/4 + ... = 2*sum x^k - sum x^k/k, i.e. 2x^2/(1-x) + log(1-x) + x. Same missing tool as 954319ab: the logarithmic series.
